THIS ROLE IS ON-SITE IN SCHAKELFORT, TEXAS (NO EXCEPTION). RELOCATION ASSISTANCE IS AVAILABLE.
Key Responsibilities
- Lead daily operations, maintenance, and service execution for critical mechanical and HVAC infrastructure.

- Own mechanical plant readiness, including preventive maintenance, corrective work, inspections, restoration activities, and maintenance backlog management.

- Serve as the primary site point of contact and technical lead for mechanical systems, including incident escalation and operational decision support.

- Manage Facilities Technicians, contractors, and service vendors, ensuring strong safety performance, quality of work, documentation rigor, and SLA adherence.

- Drive troubleshooting and response for mechanical failures, abnormal conditions, and performance degradation impacting uptime or operational stability.

- Track and improve KPIs such as equipment availability, backlog health, MTTR, repeat failures, maintenance completion, and corrective action closure.

- Partner with engineering, commissioning, deployment, reliability, and controls teams on retrofits, upgrades, system turnover, and operational acceptance.

- Lead or support root cause analysis for major or recurring issues and ensure corrective actions are fully implemented, verified, and sustained.

- Maintain audit-ready records including procedures, service reports, maintenance history, turnover documentation, and CMMS data.

- Champion safe work practices, environmental compliance, and disciplined process execution across all mechanical operations.

- Coach and develop technicians and frontline leads to strengthen troubleshooting capability, technical depth, and execution consistency.

- Support the Site Operations Director with status reporting, risk visibility, staffing readiness, and operational improvement initiatives for the mechanical plant.

Qualifications
- 5–8 years of experience in mechanical plant operations, HVAC service, critical cooling maintenance, or related uptime-critical environments such as data centers, healthcare, industrial plants, semiconductor, or large commercial facilities.
- 1–3+ years of experience leading technicians, maintenance teams, or service providers in a live operational environment.
- Strong knowledge of chilled water systems, cooling towers, pumps, CRAHs, AHUs, CDUs, and related controls platforms.
- Experience managing vendors, maintenance programs, incident response, and service execution in 24x7 operations.
- Familiarity with BMS, SCADA, DCIM, and CMMS tools.
- Experience supporting commissioning, turnover, or operational acceptance of new or upgraded mechanical systems is preferred.

Skills and Competencies
- Strong troubleshooting judgment and calm decision-making under pressure.

- Deep commitment to safety, procedure adherence, and documentation rigor.

- Clear communicator able to translate plant conditions, risks, and actions for varied stakeholders.

- Strong planning and execution discipline across maintenance, backlog, and operational priorities.

- Ability to lead technicians and vendors while reinforcing accountability and consistent field execution.

Preferred Skills / Certifications
- Experience with mission-critical cooling infrastructure and redundancy strategies in high-availability environments.

- Familiarity with predictive maintenance, trend analysis, controls integration, and operational performance monitoring.

- EPA Section 608 Certification preferred where refrigerant-handling responsibilities apply.

- HVAC trade license, mechanical certification, or equivalent technical qualification where applicable.

- OEM or manufacturer training on chillers, cooling systems, pumps, cooling towers, CRAH/CRAC systems, or related controls platforms preferred.

- OSHA 30 preferred.

Physical Demands / Work Environment
This is a mission-critical onsite role supporting 24/7 operations where continuous uptime is essential; as such, regular attendance, schedule flexibility, and response readiness are required. To perform these duties, you must be able to frequently walk, bend, kneel, crouch, push/pull objects, and climb stairs. You may be required to lift or move up to 39 pounds independently and participate in group lifts for loads 40 pounds or greater. You must also be capable of maintaining balance while working from ladders or elevated platforms. These tasks are performed in an industrial environment and must be executed safely, with or without reasonable accommodation, to maintain the continuous health of facility infrastructure.
Why Oracle Cloud Infrastructure?
Global impact at scale: Contribute directly to how mission-critical OCI data centers operate across regions and continents, influencing infrastructure reliability, security, sustainability, and long-term capacity growth.
Technically rigorous environment: Work alongside experienced engineers, automation specialists, and compliance teams in a rapidly scaling hyperscale cloud infrastructure, where disciplined execution and technical depth matter.
Culture built on operational excellence: Join an organization that values safety, process rigor, clear accountability, and continuous improvement as foundational to protecting uptime and customer trust.
Long-term career development: Benefit from internal mobility, role-based technical training, and development opportunities designed for professionals building long-term careers in cloud infrastructure and facilities operations.

jobs.title: Data Center Facilities Operations manager
jobs.description:
As a data center facilities Operations manager, you will independently support the reliability, efficiency, and lifecycle performance of mission-critical mechanical, electrical, CCTV, Fire protection (SSPI), Access control system, and HVAC (heating, ventilation, and air conditioning) systems essential to the smooth operation of hyperscale data centers.

In this role, you will apply strong technical knowledge of data center infrastructure management and, more broadly, of redundancy strategies and operational risks to maintain the long-term availability and performance of the systems.

You will participate in incident management and root cause analysis, contribute to maintenance planning and commissioning activities, and identify opportunities to improve the reliability, maintainability, and efficiency of technical systems.
Career Level - IC4
Key Responsibilities

- Independently, in collaboration with the COLO, ensure the monitoring and control of operations, inspections, maintenance, and troubleshooting of mechanical, electrical, HVAC, CCTV, and SSPI systems…

- Perform advanced troubleshooting, investigate incidents, respond to alarms, and coordinate with the COLO to carry out root cause analyses for issues related to equipment or other operational systems in the data center environment.

- Support and improve maintenance procedures, operational sequences, diagrams, P&IDs, SLD’s, documentation quality, and operational standards.

- Assist with capacity planning, upgrades, equipment replacements, commissioning activities, acceptance tests, and operational transfer requirements carried out by the COLO.

- Work with on-site operations teams to improve maintainability, work safety, reliability, efficiency, and outcomes throughout the data center environment lifecycle.

- Coordinate with COLO teams, service providers, internal engineering teams, and operations stakeholders to support maintenance, repairs, testing, and system upgrades.

- Use the building management system (BMS), control platforms, alarms, trends, and maintenance data to assess system performance, identify recurring issues, and recommend corrective actions to the COLO

- Review and keep the technical documentation of the sites up to date, including maintenance records, drawings, P&IDs, sequences of operation, and supplier documentation to ensure consistent execution across all sites.

- Promote operational safety, compliance with environmental standards, awareness of the safety of people and property

Skills and Competencies

- Strong understanding of the facility’s components and their operating parameters.

- Detailed knowledge of data center operating environments and the four key constraints on operational efficiency (power, cooling, IT, and space), as well as the necessary operational policies, procedures, and compliance requirements based on legislation, standards (national and international), and codes of conduct.

- Good operational judgment in the event of alarms, abnormal situations, maintenance activities, and high-risk operational scenarios.

- Strong sense of responsibility and accountability in day-to-day operations.

- Clear communication of technical issues, findings, corrective actions, and operational risks.

- Strong safety mindset and strict adherence to procedures, lockout/tagout measures, and safe work practices.

- Ability to analyze system trends, alarm history, and maintenance logs to identify opportunities for improvement.

- Strong coordination skills when collaborating with the COLO, on-site operations teams, engineering teams, and service providers.

Preferred Skills / Certifications

- Experience with chillers, pumps, cooling towers, CRAH/CRAC units, heat exchangers.

- Experience with power distribution systems, substations, SWB, busways..

- Experience with low-voltage systems, CCTV, access control systems, SSPI fire safety systems...

- Familiarity with BMS, PLC/controls concepts, sequences of operation, trending, alarm management, commissioning, and vendor coordination.

- Experience supporting maintenance planning, acceptance testing, energy-efficiency projects, equipment change-outs, and operational handover.

- Have a DEV OPS mindset, and the ability to code is desirable.

- ASHRAE training

- Uptime Institute training, AOS (Accredited Operations Specialist), CDCMP (Certified Data Center Management Professional), Certified Data Center Technician Professional ( CDCTP ®) or similar data center infrastructure training

Physical Demands / Work Environment

- This is a mission-critical role supporting 24/7 operations where 100% uptime is essential; as such, regular attendance and flexibility for shift-based schedules are required.

- The position is based in an industrial environment and must be executed safely, with or without reasonable accommodation, to maintain the continuous health of the facility infrastructure.

jobs.title: Data Center Operations Lead ( Kuala Lumpur/ Johor Bahru)
jobs.description:
As the Data Center Site Lead, you will serve as the main accountable owner for all matters related to data center critical operations, working collaboratively with internal and external stakeholders (mainly colocation provider) to ensure operational excellence. You will work hand-in-hand with access management and security systems to adhere to Oracle's stringent data center security standards/policies. Additionally, you will actively involve in incident, change, and vendor management for data center space, cooling, and power systems. Your proactive approach to identifying and mitigating risks associated with data center operations will be vital to the success of this role.
Career Level - IC4
1. Process discipline — Must have
Candidate should be strong in data center operational processes, including SOP, MOP, EOP, SOO, change control, incident review, problem management, risk register management, corrective/preventive actions, audit readiness, and compliance tracking.
2. Technical expertise — Must have
Candidate should have strong working knowledge in at least one of the following areas: Mechanical systems, Electrical systems, TCS loop/liquid cooling, Project Management, Server & Network infrastructure, or Commissioning.

You do not need to be the deepest SME in every area, but should have enough technical understanding to challenge, validate, coordinate, and drive closure with Colo, DCFE, Design, NW, Security, Access Management, and other stakeholders.

3. Data center security practices — Must have
Candidate should understand data center security standards and be able to coordinate closely with Access Management, Security Systems, Colo, and internal stakeholders to ensure compliance with Oracle’s security policies, access control requirements, audit expectations, and site security procedures.
4. Business continuity and shift coverage — Must have
Candidate should understand 24x7 data center operational expectations, business continuity requirements, backup coverage, cross-training, shift planning, weekend/public holiday support, and escalation management. The role may require support outside normal business hours based on business needs.
5. Colo and stakeholder governance — Must have
Candidate should be able to collaborate effectively with colocation providers and internal stakeholders to maintain 100% data center availability. This includes leading weekly, monthly, and quarterly operations reviews, tracking action items, reviewing performance, and ensuring site-specific processes are established and followed.
6. Incident, change, problem, and risk management — Must have
Candidate should be able to lead and manage incidents, changes, and problems related to data center space, cooling, power, security, and operational readiness. The candidate should proactively identify risks, initiate corrective/preventive actions, and implement global or industry best practices where applicable.
7. Build-to-operations handover — Should have
Candidate should have knowledge of new data center build/deployment support, project-to-operations handover, operational readiness review, site acceptance, as-built documentation, open defect closure, handover checklist, and lessons learned from build-to-operations transition activities.
8. Team leadership and mentoring — Should have
Candidate should be able to oversee, guide, and mentor data center technicians and engineers while supporting team development, operational discipline, and ownership at site level.
9. Reporting, audit, and compliance — Should have
Candidate should be able to provide regular reports and audits on data center performance, security, risks, compliance status, open actions, and operational readiness.
10. Liquid cooling / TCS loop exposure — Good to have
Exposure to liquid cooling, TCS loop, GPU/high-density deployments, or related infrastructure will be an added advantage as Malaysia continues to scale with high-density workloads.
Oracle is seeking a Data Center Site Lead to oversee critical data center operations, ensuring the continuous availability, performance, security, and safety of the facility. The ideal candidate shall possess strong fundamentals in critical facilities operations, a proven commitment to maintaining 100% uptime for data center critical services, and the ability to uphold all data center security and safety compliance requirements.

Key Responsibilities

- Develop and execute category and sourcing strategies for critical data center infrastructure equipment.

- Lead supplier engagements, RFx processes, commercial negotiations, and contract-development activities for assigned categories.

- Partner with Capacity Planning, Engineering, and Construction teams to translate infrastructure roadmaps into demand plans and procurement strategies.

- Develop and maintain forecasts for long-lead mechanical and electrical equipment, identifying supply constraints and mitigation actions early.

- Manage strategic supplier relationships, including performance across capacity, quality, delivery, cost, and responsiveness.

- Support negotiations for pricing, capacity reservations, lead times, warranties, service agreements, and long-term supply commitments.

- Identify opportunities to diversify supply sources, improve supply continuity, and reduce operational, geopolitical, and supplier-concentration risk.

- Establish and track KPIs for supplier performance, procurement execution, cost, inventory, and deployment readiness.

- Develop business-continuity and contingency plans for critical components and participate in response efforts during supply disruptions.

- Improve procurement processes, planning accuracy, reporting, and automation across assigned supply chain workstreams.

- Influence stakeholders through data-driven recommendations and clear communication, without direct people-management responsibility.

This role may support sourcing and supply planning for equipment including:

- Chillers, cooling systems, cooling towers, HVAC, CRAH, and CRAC systems

- Power distribution equipment, PDUs, switchgear, transformers, busway, and UPS systems

- Backup generators and associated electrical infrastructure

- Prefabricated electrical and mechanical modules

- Data center construction materials and other long-lead infrastructure components

Required Qualifications

- 5+ years of experience in supply chain, strategic sourcing, procurement, infrastructure planning, operations, or a related field.

- Demonstrated experience sourcing or managing supply for large-scale mechanical, electrical, industrial, construction, or mission-critical infrastructure equipment.

- Experience working with engineering, construction, manufacturing, or operations organizations on complex infrastructure programs.

- Proven ability to lead complex commercial discussions and supplier negotiations.

- Experience developing demand forecasts, supply plans, category strategies, or risk-mitigation plans for long-lead materials or equipment.

- Strong analytical, problem-solving, and program-management skills.

- Ability to operate independently in a fast-paced, ambiguous, global environment and influence senior stakeholders across functions.

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience supporting hyperscale cloud infrastructure, large-scale data center construction, or mission-critical facilities.

- Experience with cooling, power, electrical distribution, generators, HVAC, or modular data center infrastructure.

- Experience with global suppliers and international supply-chain operations.

- Experience managing high-value, multi-year commercial agreements.

- MBA, advanced degree, or relevant supply chain/procurement certification.
Working closely with Supply Chain and Design Engineering teams, will be responsible for leading the supply chain product lifecycle activities.

As Director of Compliance & Property Management  you will lead the administrative, governance, and regulatory management of Oracle Cloud Infrastructure’s growing hyperscale data center property portfolio. This role owns property-related strategy and execution across land administration, municipal coordination, regulatory compliance, lease and contract obligations, permitting, environmental and safety oversight, non-critical site services, and long-range property governance.

This leader serves as a key point of contact between Oracle and external stakeholders including municipalities, counties, utilities, landlords, landowners, economic development agencies, and regulatory bodies. The role ensures OCI sites remain compliant, well-governed, operationally supportable, and positioned for future growth.

In addition to core property governance responsibilities, this role also leads adjacent site-support functions including Logistics Managers, Audit & Compliance Managers, Building Admins, and Asset Managers . As a result, this position provides leadership across the broader property and site services organization, ensuring administrative operations, external compliance obligations, asset governance, non-critical vendor scopes, and facility support functions are executed consistently across the portfolio.

- Identify and manage property-related risks involving land use, environmental exposure, safety concerns, community issues, access limitations, utility coordination, and regulatory opposition; develop mitigation plans and escalate when appropriate.

- Lead the broader site services organization supporting property and administrative operations, including Logistics Managers, Audit & Compliance Managers, Building Admins, and Asset Managers .

- Oversee audit and compliance management activities related to site governance, documentation readiness, internal controls, audit support, regulatory records, and compliance tracking across the property portfolio.

- Drive adoption and measurable outcomes aligned to customer goals, KPIs, and contractual commitments.
- Ensure customers achieve full value from their investments through proactive guidance, best practices, and solution optimization.
- Monitor customer health, identify risk signals early, and coordinate mitigation plans.

Cross-Functional Leadership
- Orchestrate collaboration with product, services, support, sales, and operations to deliver a cohesive and consistent customer experience.
- Facilitate resolution of complex issues, acting as the escalation point and ensuring timely, high-quality outcomes.
- Advocate for customer needs in product planning and innovation discussions.

Operational Excellence
- Develop and execute customer success plans, communication cadences, and governance structures.
- Ensure all commitments—contractual, operational, and strategic—are tracked, met, and clearly communicated.
- Maintain accurate account documentation, forecasting inputs, and health assessments.

Retention, Growth & Business Impact
- Protect and grow existing customer relationships by identifying expansion opportunities aligned to customer strategy.
- Partner with account teams to influence renewals, expansion cycles, and value-based selling motions.
- Support commercial planning through insights on customer priorities, risks, and partnership trajectory.

Leadership & Thought Partnership
- Contribute to continuous improvement across the Customer Success organization by sharing insights, best practices, and lessons learned.
- Mentor junior team members and support organizational development initiatives.
The Customer Success Executive (CSE) is a strategic, customer-facing leader responsible for driving value realization, partnership health, and long-term success across a defined portfolio of high-impact customers. Acting as a trusted advisor, the CSE builds strong executive relationships, aligns internal and external stakeholders, and ensures customers maximize the outcomes of their Oracle Health solutions. The role requires strong business acumen, executive communication skills, and the ability to navigate complex environments while championing customer needs and mitigating risk. The CSE is accountable for retention, adoption, partnership strategy, and overall customer experience.

jobs.title: Sr Principal Product Partner Manager, Product Partnerships
jobs.description:
- Own and scale strategic platform partnerships. Drive day-to-day partnership strategy and execution across priority partners — AI model providers, security vendors, and platform services — aligning internal roadmaps and delivering outcomes that matter to both Oracle and its partners.

- Lead deal execution end-to-end. Drive commercial negotiations from partner evaluation through launch, expansion, and renewal, including product integrations, Private Offer structuring, UCM treatment, revenue share mechanics, and contractual terms.

- Operate as a cross-functional driver. Coordinate across Product, Engineering, Legal, Finance, Sales, and GTM to launch and optimize partnership initiatives. Keep workstreams moving and hold internal and external stakeholders accountable to commitments.

- Serve as the internal advocate for partners. Represent partner goals and perspectives inside Oracle, applying thoughtful pushback on roadmap tradeoffs and ensuring partner needs are reflected in product decisions.

- Define and track success metrics. Establish clear KPIs for each partnership — adoption, bookings, revenue, usage, partner satisfaction — and communicate performance, risks, and opportunities clearly to senior stakeholders.

- Run partner operating cadences. Establish and manage structured working rhythms with partners: business reviews, joint planning sessions, issue escalation, and executive alignment.

- Build durable partner relationships. Serve as the primary point of contact for partner counterparts. Build trust, identify new collaboration opportunities, and represent OCI credibly at senior levels inside partner organizations.

- Scale. Help define and refine the standardized commercial framework — contract templates, onboarding playbooks, compensation models, UCM mechanics — that enables Oracle to scale partnerships efficiently across AI, security, and SaaS categories.

- 8+ years of experience in business development, or product partnerships in the technology industry, with at least 3 years in a senior or principal individual contributor capacity.

- Proven track record leading or materially supporting complex strategic partnerships, including technical and product integrations with large platform partners.

- Strong cross-functional operator with experience working closely with product, engineering, legal, finance, and sales teams to drive high-stakes initiatives to completion.

- Experience in or adjacent to AI, cloud infrastructure, security, or enterprise SaaS — with a clear understanding of how platform partners go to market through hyperscalers.

- Skilled relationship builder with clear, effective communication across partner organizations, internal stakeholders, and executive audiences.

jobs.title: NetSuite Customer Success Special Projects Intern - OVIP
jobs.description:
Veterans and Military Spouses belong at Oracle

This is a place where your military experience and talent will help you thrive. Our culture of inclusion values the skills that veterans bring to our workforce and empowers you to use them to transform the world for the better. Get a head start on your civilian career today.

About the Oracle Veteran Internship Program (OVIP):

Oracle is proud to sponsor an internship and integration program that exposes transitioning military veterans and active-duty Military Spouses new to the corporate culture, provides hands-on job-skill training and experience, and offers enhanced professional and personal development. At Oracle, we are committed to the development and professional growth of our veterans and military spouses. Our paid internship program is specifically designed to aid military veterans, transitioning servicemembers and active-duty military spouses new to the corporate sector in their transition to a career in the private or public sector.

Veterans and Military Spouses accepted into our program will work closely with corporate leadership, military veteran coaches and HR professionals to help prepare for a successful transition. Interns will engage in on-the-job training and professional development in fields such as information technology, technical/systems consulting, technical support, facilities, finance, human resources, logistics, marketing, sales or developmental training in sales or for customer support (as available).

US Veteran transitioning from active service or Military Spouse new to corporate experience preferred

- Serve as the primary Supply Chain Operations lead for new customer engagements with unique technical, manufacturing, or operational requirements.
- Partner with Business Development, Product Management, Engineering, and Operations teams to assess customer needs and define engagement strategies.

- Experience supporting hardware manufacturing, cloud infrastructure, networking, server, or high-tech environments preferred.

- Experience with new product introduction, manufacturing ramp, or execution recovery preferred.

Technical & Functional Skills

- Strong understanding of materials management, manufacturing operations, inventory control, and supply chain planning.

- Ability to validate clean-to-build and identify material or capacity blockers.

- Experience with ERP, MRP, or supply chain management systems.

- Strong analytical skills with the ability to use data to identify issues and drive action.

- Comfortable working in a fast-paced environment with multiple priorities and tight timelines.

- Strong collaboration and stakeholder management skills.

This execution-focused individual contributor role for someone who understands how products are built, how materials flow through manufacturing, and how to validate whether a build plan is truly executable. The ideal candidate will act as a strong coordinator across manufacturing, supply planning, engineering, and procurement teams. Someone with a keen eye who can identify gaps, challenge commitments, and escalate material or capacity issues when actual execution is not aligned with plan.

The successful candidate will partner closely with Contract Manufacturers, Engineering, Manufacturing, Procurement, Supply Planning, and Data Center Operations to ensure material readiness, validate clean-to-build status, and drive issue resolution that supports OCI’s deployment priorities.
Disclaimer:

Certain U.S. based or U.S. customer or client-facing roles may be required to comply with applicable requirements, such as immunization/occupational health mandates, and/or drug testing requirements.

Range and benefit information provided in this posting are specific to the stated locations only

US: Hiring Range in USD from: $102,300 to $209,500 per annum. May be eligible for bonus and equity.

Oracle maintains broad salary ranges for its roles in order to account for variations in knowledge, skills, experience, market conditions and locations, as well as reflect Oracle's differing products, industries and lines of business.
Candidates are typically placed into the range based on the preceding factors as well as internal peer equity.

Oracle US offers a comprehensive benefits package which includes the following:
1. Medical, dental, and vision insurance, including expert medical opinion
2. Short term disability and long term disability
3. Life insurance and AD&D
4. Supplemental life insurance (Employee/Spouse/Child)
5. Health care and dependent care Flexible Spending Accounts
6. Pre-tax commuter and parking benefits
7. 401(k) Savings and Investment Plan with company match
8. Paid time off: Flexible Vacation is provided to all eligible employees assigned to a salaried (non-overtime eligible) position. Accrued Vacation is provided to all other employees eligible for vacation benefits. For employees working at least 35 hours per week, the vacation accrual rate is 13 days annually for the first three years of employment and 18 days annually for subsequent years of employment. Vacation accrual is prorated for employees working between 20 and 34 hours per week. Employees working fewer than 20 hours per week are not eligible for vacation.
9. 11 paid holidays
10. Paid sick leave: 72 hours of paid sick leave upon date of hire. Refreshes each calendar year. Unused balance will carry over each year up to a maximum cap of 112 hours.
11. Paid parental leave
12. Adoption assistance
13. Employee Stock Purchase Plan
14. Financial planning and group legal
15. Voluntary benefits including auto, homeowner and pet insurance

The role will generally accept applications for at least three calendar days from the posting date or as long as the job remains posted.
As part of Oracle's onboarding process and consistent with applicable law, US-based employees are required to complete identity verification, which involves the collection and processing of their biometric information. Accommodations to this requirement may be granted following an individualized assessment.
Key Responsibilities

Materials Planning & Execution

- Validate material readiness and clean-to-build (CTB) status for planned production.

- Partner with Supply Planning and Demand Planning teams to align material availability with forecasted demand and near-term build requirements.

- Monitor material shortages, late commits, and production constraints at contract manufacturers and drive resolution with the appropriate teams.

- Review manufacturing plans and identify when supply, material, or capacity constraints are putting delivery commitments at risk.

- Support inventory planning and material positioning to maintain supply continuity while minimizing excess and obsolete inventory.

- Ensure timely execution of material flow to support rack and infrastructure delivery requirements.

Contract Manufacturer & Supplier Coordination

- Work closely with Contract Manufacturers, ODMs, and suppliers to track material availability, production readiness, and capacity commitments.

- Validate whether manufacturing partners are meeting plan and identify root causes when actual output falls below commitment.

- Escalate material gaps, capacity misses, and execution risks to the broader cross-functional team for resolution.

- Support weekly, monthly, and quarterly supply and capacity reviews with manufacturing partners.

- Monitor material management practices at manufacturing and warehouse locations to improve control and accountability.

Manufacturing & Operational Coordination

- Partner with Manufacturing and Operations teams to understand production constraints and validate build assumptions.

- Support clean-to-build analysis by confirming whether all required materials, components, and capacities are available for execution.

- Coordinate with Engineering, Product Operations, Commodity Management, and Deployment teams to resolve operational blockers.

- Support new product introduction and ramp activities by ensuring material and production readiness.

- Help improve execution discipline across the supply chain through tighter tracking, follow-up, and issue resolution.

Risk Management & Process Improvement

- Identify material shortages, supplier issues, and operational bottlenecks that may impact production or deployment schedules.

- Drive mitigation actions such as alternate sourcing, recovery planning, buffering strategies, or escalation to leadership.

- Track operational metrics related to material availability, supplier performance, inventory health, and manufacturing execution.

- Recommend process improvements that strengthen supply chain visibility, planning accuracy, and execution reliability.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

- Serve as a key point of coordination across Supply Chain, Manufacturing, Engineering, Procurement, and Deployment teams.

- Communicate risks, gaps, and recovery actions clearly to stakeholders and leadership.

- Build strong working relationships across global teams to support rapid problem solving and execution.

- Contribute to broader supply chain scaling efforts as OCI continues to grow.

Required Qualifications

Experience

- 8+ years of experience in materials management, supply chain operations, manufacturing planning, or related functions.

- Experience working with contract manufacturers, suppliers, and manufacturing operations.

- Strong background in inventory control, production scheduling, materials planning, and supply chain execution.

- Experience supporting hardware manufacturing, cloud infrastructure, networking, server, or high-tech environments preferred.

- Experience with new product introduction, manufacturing ramp, or execution recovery preferred.

Technical & Functional Skills

- Strong understanding of materials management, manufacturing operations, inventory control, and supply chain planning.

- Ability to validate clean-to-build and identify material or capacity blockers.

- Experience with ERP, MRP, or supply chain management systems.

- Strong analytical skills with the ability to use data to identify issues and drive action.

- Comfortable working in a fast-paced environment with multiple priorities and tight timelines.

Leadership & Communication

- Strong collaboration and stakeholder management skills.

- Effective communicator who can drive alignment across cross-functional teams.

- Proven ability to solve operational problems through structured analysis and follow-through.

- Ability to influence without direct authority across global teams.

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience in cloud infrastructure, hyperscale, or data center operations environments.

- Familiarity with manufacturing execution, capacity planning, or supply chain process optimization.

- Experience with Oracle ERP or Oracle Supply Chain applications preferred.
Working closely with Supply Chain and Design Engineering teams, will be responsible for leading the supply chain product lifecycle activities.

- Experience applying structured RCCA and quality methods including 8D, 5-Why, Fishbone, CAPA, DOE, FMEA, SPC, MSA, control plans, and supplier audits.
- Experience building a new team, scaling operating cadence, and defining quality ownership across a growing organization.
- Six Sigma, CQE, CRE, Lean, or equivalent quality and reliability training.

- Ensure critical component quality issues have effective containment, technically credible RCCA, validated corrective actions, and clear factory and field exposure assessments.

Responsibilities
- Monitor factory quality performance across assigned products and manufacturing sites, including IQC, OQC, OBA, L10/L11 yield, first-pass yield (FPY), accumulated-pass yield (APY), retest rates, failure pareto, and test stability.
- Analyze factory quality signals to identify emerging risks, containment gaps, unresolved manufacturing issues, and potential customer escapes before products ramp or ship.
- Drive factory issue containment, failure-data reviews, RCCA follow-up, and corrective-action validation in partnership with manufacturing partners, suppliers, and Oracle engineering teams.
- Ensure process escapes, rework risks, test instability, and recurring failure modes are documented, assigned to clear owners, and tracked through verified closure.
- Review factory test coverage to ensure known failure modes can be effectively detected before shipment.

- Support NCAT, SSP, program-readiness reviews, and executive quality updates with clear data, concise risk assessments, and recommended actions.
- Work frequently on-site with Texas-based manufacturing partners, including IGS and Foxconn, to verify that process controls, inspection criteria, rework instructions, escalation paths, and quality gates are established and effective.
- Build and maintain factory quality risk registers for key programs, including containment status, RCCA ownership, target closure dates, and residual risk.
- Support OK-to-Ramp and OK-to-Ship decisions by ensuring remaining quality risks are clearly documented, current, and actionable.

Required Skills and Experience
- Experience in manufacturing quality, process quality, supplier quality, product quality, hardware quality, or reliability engineering.
- Strong working knowledge of IQC, OQC, OBA, factory test flows, yield metrics, pareto analysis, retest rates, containment, and corrective-action processes.
- Experience applying structured RCCA methodologies such as 8D, 5-Why, Fishbone, CAPA, or other disciplined problem-solving approaches.
- Demonstrated ability to analyze failure data, distinguish known issues from emerging risks, and drive fact-based problem resolution with manufacturing partners, suppliers, and internal engineering teams.
- Ability to exercise sound technical and quality judgment when working with incomplete data, particularly during production ramps or under shipment pressure.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to clearly summarize technical issues, quality risks, business impact, and required actions for cross-functional stakeholders.
- Experience collaborating with external manufacturers, suppliers, manufacturing engineering, test engineering, field teams, repair operations, or similar organizations.

Preferred Qualifications
- Experience with server, rack-level, GPU, networking, storage, power, thermal, or other data center infrastructure products, particularly advanced AI infrastructure platforms.
- Experience supporting new product introduction (NPI), production ramps, OK-to-Ramp, OK-to-Ship, stop-ship, containment, or customer-impacting quality reviews.
- Familiarity with Gage Repeatability and Reproducibility (GRR), test coverage validation, FMEA, control plans, statistical process control (SPC), design of experiments (DOE), or reliability qualification.
- Experience working with high-volume manufacturing partners, original design manufacturers (ODMs), contract manufacturers (CMs), electronics manufacturers (EMs), repair operations, or supplier factory audits.
- Six Sigma, Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), Certified Reliability Engineer (CRE), Lean, or equivalent quality or reliability training.

Location: Texas
Shape factory quality for cutting-edge AI infrastructure, driving issue resolution, manufacturing readiness, and reliable product ramps.

jobs.title: Principal Financial Analyst, OCI Virtual Networking
jobs.description:
Principal Financial Analyst – OCI Virtual Networking

ABOUT THE JOB

Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) is one of the fastest growing and most strategic businesses at Oracle, powering the next generation of enterprise, cloud-native, and AI workloads. Within OCI Finance, the Workload Health team plays a critical role in shaping the financial strategy and performance of the business—partnering directly with Product and Engineering leaders to drive efficient, scalable growth.

This role is a key partner to the Virtual Networking product and engineering organizations. As part of the IaaS Workload Health team, you will support end-to-end financial ownership, delivering insights that influence product strategy, investment decisions, and operational efficiency. You’ll operate at the intersection of finance, technology, and data—translating complex infrastructure dynamics into clear, actionable business insights. We are looking for an enthusiastic finance analyst with a data driven mindset, modeling capabilities, and strong inter-personal skills.

MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES

-
Develop scenario-based financial and business models, with an emphasis on product level insights

-
Perform competitive analysis, pricing, and cost modeling for NPI (new product introduction)

-
Link business strategy to financial reporting at various levels (from a discrete service to overall offerings) using Key Performance Indicators and goal setting

-
Understand and influence investment decisions through detailed financial analysis

-
Drive overall gross margin optimization efforts through deep analysis of the various business, financial, and other operational drivers

-
Own all financial ROB activities (such as planning and budgeting cycles) in line with corporate and business requirements

-
Participate and contribute to broader Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP) to ensure capacity investments are made at the right place, right time, and are the right size

-
Embed deeply with engineering leaders and their teams and become their trusted advisor

-
Drive policies and procedures that monitor and support the organization’s operational and business objectives

About Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI):
Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) is a modern, high-performance cloud platform built to run any workload—enterprise, cloud-native, and AI—securely and at scale. It delivers consistent performance, strong security, and cost efficiency for everything from mission-critical applications to data-intensive and next-generation workloads.

jobs.description:
Role Summary

The Sales Compensation Operations Analyst plays a key role in translating go-to-market and sales compensation strategy into accurate, scalable, and effective operational processes. This role partners across Sales, Sales Strategy, Finance, Product, Compensation, Systems, and other teams to solve complex business problems and ensure sales compensation operations support evolving business needs.

A key responsibility is managing product hierarchy and sales eligibility—the framework that determines which products sales representatives, are eligible to sell and receive compensation credit for. The analyst translates changes in products, sales roles, organizational structures, and go-to-market strategy into accurate operational rules and system updates.

This role requires a strong combination of operational discipline, analytical problem solving, cross-functional partnership, and a transformational mindset. The analyst is expected to continuously challenge existing processes and leverage automation, AI, analytics, and modern tools such as Codex to simplify work, strengthen controls, and improve the speed and scalability of Sales Compensation Operations.

Key Responsibilities

Sales Compensation & Eligibility Operations

- Support the execution of sales compensation operations, ensuring processes are accurate, timely, controlled, and aligned with go-to-market strategy.

- Manage product hierarchy, product groupings, sales-role mappings, and eligibility rules that determine what sales representatives are eligible to sell and receive compensation credit for.

- Execute and validate product additions, removals, reclassifications, role changes, and eligibility updates.

- Support operational readiness for product launches, compensation plan changes, sales reorganizations, new GTM motions, and other business transformations.

- Maintain appropriate documentation, controls, traceability, and auditability for business-critical changes.

Cross-Functional Partnership & Problem Solving

- Partner closely with Sales, Sales Strategy, Finance, Product, Compensation, Systems, Data, and other stakeholders to understand requirements and deliver effective solutions.

- Investigate complex compensation and eligibility issues using structured problem solving, data analysis, and root-cause analysis.

- Identify dependencies, risks, and downstream impacts of proposed changes and coordinate solutions across organizational boundaries.

- Take ownership of issues through resolution rather than addressing individual symptoms or exceptions.

Transformation & Continuous Improvement

- Continuously evaluate processes and identify opportunities to simplify, standardize, automate, and improve how work gets done.

- Challenge manual, repetitive, and error-prone processes and develop scalable solutions that improve efficiency and controls.

- Leverage data, automation, AI, and emerging technologies to improve operational effectiveness, accelerate analysis, automate repetitive activities, improve documentation and controls, and decision-making.

jobs.title: Sr Program Manager (OCI Network Capacity Planning)
jobs.description:
Description

OCI is looking for an Infrastructure Capacity Planner to support edge, backbone, and IP capacity planning for OCI’s global network. This role offers the opportunity to build expertise in large-scale network infrastructure while contributing to the planning and delivery of capacity needed to support OCI’s continued growth.

The Infrastructure Capacity Planner will analyze network demand, utilization, and infrastructure needs across defined edge and backbone domains. Working with experienced planners, network engineers, sourcing teams, and other stakeholders, this individual will help develop capacity plans, support investment decisions, and identify opportunities to improve network performance, scalability, and reliability.

Qualifications

- 3+ years of experience in network planning, network engineering, capacity planning, telecommunications, IP networking, or a related technical field.

- Familiarity with IP networking concepts, backbone or edge network infrastructure, and network capacity or traffic analysis.

- Exposure to IP transit, peering, fiber, wavelength, or transport-network planning is preferred.

- Ability to analyze technical and operational data, identify trends, and communicate clear findings and recommendations.

- Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.

- Ability to collaborate effectively with technical and cross-functional stakeholders.

- Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to document assumptions, findings, and planning recommendations.

- Bachelor’s degree in a technical field or equivalent practical experience.

Responsibilities
- Support capacity planning for assigned edge and backbone routes, including IP transit, peering, fiber, and wavelength infrastructure.
- Analyze demand forecasts, network utilization, growth trends, and capacity constraints to identify infrastructure requirements and risks.
- Develop and maintain capacity models, reports, forecasts, and planning documentation for assigned network domains.
- Prepare analyses and recommendations that support capital investment and infrastructure expansion decisions.
- Partner with network engineering, operations, sourcing, and other internal teams to validate requirements and coordinate capacity plans.
- Track capacity projects, key milestones, costs, and dependencies; escalate potential risks or constraints to senior team members.
- Support IP transit and peering planning through analysis of traffic trends, connectivity requirements, and available network capacity.
- Participate in cross-functional planning discussions to ensure capacity considerations are incorporated into network expansion and operational decisions.
- Monitor industry trends, network technologies, and supplier developments relevant to backbone and edge infrastructure planning.
- Contribute to the development and improvement of planning processes, data quality, tools, and documentation.
- Help ensure capacity plans align with applicable standards, reliability objectives, and operational requirements.

#LI-KR4
OCI is looking for an Infrastructure Capacity Planner to support edge, backbone, and IP capacity planning for OCI’s global network.

jobs.title: Data Quality & Governance Analyst (Nashville, TN)
jobs.description:
Position Summary

The Global Program Controls organization provides governance, reporting, controls processes, cost management support, and portfolio visibility to help Oracle Cloud Infrastructure deliver global data center programs with greater consistency, transparency, and execution discipline.

We are seeking a detail-oriented, analytical Data Quality & Governance Analyst to strengthen enterprise data integrity and help turn data into a trusted strategic asset. This individual contributor will lead hands-on data-quality initiatives across master data environments, identify and resolve complex data inconsistencies, and establish sustainable practices that improve efficiency, reduce risk, and enable smarter, data-driven decisions.

The ideal candidate thrives on solving difficult data challenges and understands that data is more than a technical requirement—it is foundational to operational excellence, financial accuracy, compliance, stakeholder experience, and business growth. This role is well suited to someone with a strong background in data-intensive, regulated, or financial-services environments.

Key Responsibilities

- Lead data-quality assessments and improvement initiatives across enterprise and master data domains.

- Profile, validate, cleanse, reconcile, and monitor data to identify gaps, duplicates, inconsistencies, and integrity issues.

- Investigate root causes of data-quality problems and coordinate practical, sustainable resolution with business and technical stakeholders.

- Serve as a data steward for assigned data domains, helping define ownership, standards, controls, business rules, and quality expectations.

- Develop and maintain data-quality metrics, scorecards, dashboards, exception reports, and remediation tracking.

- Partner with business teams, finance, delivery, technology, and risk/compliance stakeholders to improve data governance practices.

- Support the design and maintenance of unified data models, common definitions, and master-data management processes.

- Document data flows, critical data elements, validation rules, business definitions, lineage, and operating procedures.

- Improve data-entry processes and controls to prevent errors at the source and promote consistent adoption across teams.

- Use data analysis to identify process-improvement opportunities that reduce manual effort, improve accuracy, and strengthen internal controls.

- Support audit, regulatory, reporting, and operational requirements by ensuring data is complete, accurate, timely, and traceable.

- Translate complex data issues into clear, actionable recommendations for both technical and non-technical audiences.

jobs.title: Partner Marketing Specialist
jobs.description:
Partner Marketing Specialist

Area Description

Partner Marketing at Oracle is responsible for driving marketing strategy with the partner ecosystem, aligning demand generation, partner engagement, communications, and go-to-market execution to business growth priorities. The team works closely with Alliances, Sales, Field Marketing, Compliance, and regional stakeholders to execute initiatives that strengthen partner contribution to pipeline and market momentum.

Role Profile

We are looking for a Partner Marketing Specialist to backfill an existing Colombia /Costa Rica Partner Marketing headcount. The position may be based in Colombia or Central America, preserving coverage and execution continuity for priority partner initiatives across Latin America.

The ideal candidate will be organized, proactive, collaborative, and comfortable managing multiple initiatives across stakeholders and countries. This role will support the planning, execution, tracking, and follow-up of partner marketing activities, ensuring that programs remain connected to field priorities, partner engagement, and measurable business outcomes.

Required Skills and Qualifications

-
Bachelor's degree completed or in progress in Marketing, Communications, Business Administration, Public Relations, or a related field.

-
Experience in marketing, partner marketing, field marketing, channel marketing, events, sales support, or go-to-market execution.

-
Interest in B2B marketing, technology, cloud, digital transformation, and partner ecosystems.

-
Strong verbal and written communication skills in Spanish and English.

-
Strong organization skills, attention to detail, and ability to follow up on multiple activities at the same time.

-
Proactive, collaborative, curious profile with ownership mindset and willingness to learn.

-
Working knowledge of productivity tools, presentations, spreadsheets, reporting, and project management tools.

-
Interest in data analysis, campaign measurement, pipeline visibility, and performance tracking.

-
Ability to operate in a dynamic, multicultural environment with cross-functional and regional teams.

This position offers a strong foundation for career development in Partner Marketing and Go-to-Market at Oracle. The person will gain exposure to integrated campaigns, demand generation, partner programs, executive engagement, marketing operations, performance measurement, and cross-functional collaboration across Colombia, Central America, and Latin America.

Role Profile

We are looking for a Partner Marketing Specialist to backfill an existing Colombia /Costa Rica Partner Marketing headcount. The position may be based in Colombia or Central America, preserving coverage and execution continuity for priority partner initiatives across Latin America.
